questions.prompt: Where is the Moon at new moon?
options: On the opposite side of Earth from the Sun
At right angles to the Sun
questions.explain: Its sunlit side faces away from us.

questions.prompt: A Moon that is half lit on the RIGHT side (as seen from India) is at…
questions.explain: Waxing phases are lit on the right in the northern hemisphere.

questions.prompt: Which TWO conditions are needed for a lunar eclipse?
questions.explain: Full moon + node = the Moon passes through Earth's shadow.

questions.prompt: A thin crescent Moon is seen low in the west just after sunset. Is it waxing or waning?
questions.explain: The evening crescent is a few days after new moon, so it is growing.

questions.prompt: Diwali is celebrated on Amavasya. Could a lunar eclipse ever happen on Diwali night?
options: No: lunar eclipses happen only at full moon
questions.explain: Amavasya is new moon; a SOLAR eclipse is possible, but never a lunar one.

questions.prompt: Explain, with the positions of the Sun, Earth and Moon, why a lunar eclipse can be seen from the whole night side of Earth, but a total solar eclipse only from a narrow strip.
questions.modelAnswer: In a lunar eclipse, the Moon moves into Earth's large shadow. Anyone on the night side who can see the Moon sees it darken. In a solar eclipse, the Moon is much smaller than Earth, so its shadow on Earth is small; only people inside that small shadow (a narrow path as Earth turns) see the Sun completely covered, while nearby places see a partial eclipse.
rubric: Lunar: the Moon enters Earth’s big shadow, seen by the whole night side
Solar: the Moon's small shadow falls on a small area
questions.explain: Criterion C: explain with a model.

questions.prompt: Full moon was on the 1st of a month. Roughly which date will the next full moon be (in a 31-day month)?

questions.text: In a ___ eclipse the Moon blocks the Sun; in a ___ eclipse the Earth’s shadow covers the Moon.
questions.explain: Solar = Sun hidden; lunar = Moon darkened.
